title: Logarithmic transport at topological phase transitions of one-dimensional chiral quantum systems
abstract: The random hopping Hamiltonian is a toy model for a disorder-driven topological phase transitions in one-dimensional chiral Hamiltonians. It has a vanishing Lyapunov exponent and a Dyson peak in the density of states at zero energy. This work shows how the quantum dynamics leads to a logarithmic growth of the moments of the position operator, similar as in classical Sinai diffusion. The mechanism at the origin of this phenomenon is that the eigenfunction of the smallest eigenvalue is well-approximated by the exponential of a classical random walk, leading to two essentially independent subexponential localization centers.
summary: This paper analyzes quantum transport in disordered, one-dimensional chiral quantum systems near topological phase transitions. It proves that the quantum dynamics cause the position moments to grow logarithmically with time, mirroring classical Sinai diffusion. The analysis achieves this by relating the system's lowest energy eigenstate to the exponential of a random walk.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantum dynamics and transport properties at disorder-driven topological phase transitions in one-dimensional chiral quantum systems.
main_result: The quantum dynamics leads to a logarithmic growth of the moments of the position operator, similar to classical Sinai diffusion, providing a rigorous lower bound for this transport.
method: The analysis uses spectral theory, approximating the lowest energy eigenfunction by the exponential of a random walk, and deriving lower bounds for time-averaged position moments.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a random hopping Hamiltonian ($H_N$), which serves as a toy model for disorder-driven topological phase transitions in quasi-one-dimensional chiral Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Time- and disorder-averaged $q$-th moments of the position operator ($M_N^q(T)$), the smallest positive eigenvalue ($E_{N,1}$), and the eigenfunction components ($\phi_E$).
important_parameters: The time scale $T$ is analyzed in a specific regime, $e^{c_1 N^\alpha} \le T \le e^{c_2 N^\alpha}$, and the system size $N$ is crucial.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on approximating the eigenstate by the exponential of a random walk and focusing on the diagonal terms in the moment expansion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial profile of the smallest eigenvalue eigenfunction and associated random walks, and compare the distributions of the maximal eigenfunction values against zero-energy state predictions.
paper_structure: The work progresses by analyzing the spectral properties of the chiral Hamiltonian, establishing the relationship between the eigenstate and random walks, and finally deriving a rigorous lower bound for the position moments using these approximations.
why_interesting: The connection between quantum transport, localization phenomena, and classical diffusion models (Sinai) in the presence of disorder is highly relevant to understanding energy transport in disordered quantum materials.
